bib.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data

question: How can a router learned from human preference data choose between a strong and a weak LLM per query to cut cost while keeping response quality?
hypothesis: Routers trained on Chatbot Arena preference data, augmented with golden-label or LLM-judge data, can route queries and generalise to unseen benchmarks and model pairs.
contributions: A learning framework for routers using human preference data and data augmentation, over 2x cost savings with minimal quality loss
Routers generalise to unseen data and to multiple LLM pairs
Open-source framework for training, serving and evaluating routers

method.summary: Binary router predicts P(strong wins | query) from preference data with four parameterisations (similarity-weighted BT ranking, matrix factorisation, BERT, Llama 3 8B) and thresholds it at alpha. Trained on Chatbot Arena tiers, optionally augmented with MMLU-validation golden labels or GPT-4-judged Nectar queries; evaluated on MT Bench, MMLU, GSM8K against a random router.
method.task: binary LLM routing (strong vs weak) by predicted win probability

datasets.name: Chatbot Arena battles (D_arena)
datasets.size: 80k battles; 5k held out for validation; after pruning prompts under 16 characters, 65k pairwise comparisons between 64 models
datasets.preprocessing: Models clustered into 10 tiers by leaderboard score (dynamic programming); top two tiers = strong, tier three = weak; responses dropped, only winner identity kept. 81% English, 3.1% Chinese, 2.2% Russian.

datasets.name: MMLU validation (D_gold)
datasets.preprocessing: labels from comparing Ms and Mw answers to the golden label

datasets.name: Nectar GPT-4-judged (D_judge)
datasets.source: Nectar (Zhu et al. 2023) queries with GPT-4 responses as Ms; Mixtral-8x7B responses as Mw; GPT-4 judge
datasets.preprocessing: judge de-biased following Zheng et al. 2023

datasets.name: MT Bench
datasets.preprocessing: embedding-similarity decontamination at 0.95 threshold, contaminated eval examples discarded

models.name: Similarity-weighted ranking router
models.architecture: Bradley-Terry with similarity weights gamma^(1+S), gamma=10, text-embedding-3-small embeddings

models.name: Matrix factorization router
models.architecture: bilinear delta(M,q)=w2^T(v_m ⊙ (W1^T v_q + b)), text-embedding-3-small query embeddings

models.name: BERT classifier router
models.architecture: BERT-base with logistic head on CLS

models.name: Causal LLM router
models.architecture: Llama 3 8B, label tokens added to vocabulary, softmax over win/tie/lose labels

other.role: unseen strong/weak pairs, routers not retrained

training.objective: maximise sum log P_theta(l_sw | q) over preference data (Eq 1); BT uses weighted binary cross-entropy
training.weight_decay: matrix factorization 1e-5; BERT 0.01; Llama 3 8B not stated

inference.samples: not stated; random baseline reported with 95% CI
inference.prompting: MMLU 5-shot, GSM8K 8-shot; Llama 3 router uses an instruction prompt containing the query (text not given)

parameters.threshold alpha: swept to hit cost constraints c_i, 10 discretisation points over the call-percentage interval

metrics.name: CPT(x%)
metrics.definition: minimum percentage of calls to the strong model to reach PGR x%

baselines: Unify AI and Martian commercial routers (Appendix E, Fig 2, with gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 as strong)
eval.protocol: Evaluated on decontaminated MT Bench (GPT-4 judge), MMLU, GSM8K; no seeds stated

availability.code: open sourced framework (no URL in text)

limits: Real-world query distributions may differ substantially from these benchmarks (authors concede)
Only two-model routing; multi-model extension left to future work
Performance across routers trained on the same data varies widely on one benchmark without clear explanation (authors concede)
High-capacity routers (BERT, causal LLM) near random on Arena alone, low-data regime
Hyperparameters like optimizer for BERT/Llama, seeds, schedules, warmup and matrix-factorization dimensions not stated; no code URL in text
Quality scores for MT Bench use GPT-4 judge; MMLU/GSM8K evaluated on the Ms/Mw pair gpt-4-1106 / Mixtral; prices dated 2024

terms.definition: performance gap recovered: how much of the performance difference between the weak and strong models is recovered by the router
call-performance threshold: minimum percentage of calls to the strong model needed to reach a desired PGR

code.snippet: R_alpha(q) = M_weak if P(win_s | q) < alpha; M_strong if P(win_s | q) >= alpha
